en: Svapnādhyāya.
Homage to the Buddha! Svapnādhyāya.
Homage to the Buddha!
I shall proclaim the chapter on dreams composed by Bṛhaspati, by which the auspicious and inauspicious [results] for men are known within their dreams. (1)
A dream in the first watch yields its fruit within a year;
in the second, within eight months; and in the third, within three months. ||2||
But by four [repetitions], the fruit shall be firmly secured for men in the fourth [birth];
at the time of dawn, the fruit shall be attained within ten days. (3)

Blows from weapons, a body filled with worms, being cast down in battle, the crushing of limbs, smearing with excrement, the flow of blood, sexual intercourse with forbidden women, and grain—[these are seen] in dreams. (4)
Climbing onto a bull, an elephant, a palace, a mountain peak, or a tree;
or boarding a boat, taking up a lute, eating, or weeping—these portend the certain attainment of wealth. (5)
But he who sees at the end of a dream a king, an elephant, a horse,
gold, a bull, or a cow— his household prospers.
If a single tree that bears both milk and fruit grows alone,
and one who stays there awakens [to its presence], he shall quickly obtain wealth.
But he who, having eaten while staying in a palace, drinks water at the edge of the ocean—even if born in the family of a slave—he too shall become a king. (8)
He who sees at the end of a dream a lamp, food, fruit, a maiden, an umbrella, a chariot, or a banner, certainly obtains those very things. ||9||
If one should eat human flesh at the end of a dream, there is a gain of five hundred [gold pieces] for eating a foot, and a thousand for eating an arm. 10.
By eating the head, one who possesses a meritorious body obtains a kingdom;
moreover, such a man may even become the lord of many crores. ||11||
He who encircles a house or cities with missiles shall become the sovereign of a circle of kingdoms within that house, or a king within that city. ||12||
He who, having obtained a pair of sandals and an umbrella,
perceives them as a stainless and sharp sword, possesses prosperity that faces every direction.
One who has embarked on a boat may meet with disaster, yet he shall also emerge from it;
one should predict his journey abroad and his swift return. ||14||
He who, at the end of a dream, mounts a donkey, a camel, or a horse known to him, even while remaining there, awakens and attains sovereignty. ||15||
He whose teeth fall out and grow back again, or fall away, shall suffer the loss of kinsmen and his offspring shall perish. (16)
But if [the bird] is smeared with oil, fat, and ghee, one should diagnose it as being afflicted by disease. ||17||
A being wearing red garments is led toward the southern direction;
if he is seized by the hand by a dark-complexioned woman, one should predict his death. 18.
He who in a dream embraces a woman wearing red garments and anointed with red perfumes will not see the night of the west [i.e., he will die]. 19.
For him who embraces in a dream a woman wearing white garments and anointed with white perfumes, prosperity faces every direction. 20.
If anyone, while sleeping at night, is bitten by leeches, a daughter will be born to him; there is no need for further deliberation on this matter. ||21||
If horned or tusked beasts, or even monkeys or Rāhus, attack one in a dream, there will be danger from the royal family. 22.
If one sees the orb of the sun or the moon in a dream, he obtains a treasury from men, or they bestow a house upon him. ||23||
Furthermore, he who is bound with fetters or even with the noose of his own arms will have either a son born to him or his established position will be pointed out [as lost]. ||24||
He who will bite the heated iron image on his right arm shall obtain a thousandfold profit on the completion of the tenth day. 25.
If a Brāhmaṇa drinks blood or even liquor in any way whatsoever during a dream, he incurs a debt; any other person incurs a loss of wealth. ||26||
If one sees milk with foam coming from a milch cow in a dream, that person will have the drinking of soma, or one should predict some other form of prosperity for him. ||27||
By giving curd, one gains affection; by wheat, the arrival of wealth;
by barley, one should know the attainment of sacrifice; and by white mustard seeds, there is gain as well. 28.
When [the enemy] is in bloom, one should cause one's own undertaking to blossom; when he has borne fruit, one should seek the highest prosperity for oneself;
when he is smoking, one should smoke; and when he is blazing, one should expect wealth.
Whether on a seat, in a bed, or even upon his body, vehicle, or house, when these appear as if ablaze, one should wake up; for him, prosperity faces every direction. ||30||
He is freed from disease and free from suffering.
